name: Morrill Hall
use: Formerly agriculture/horticulture, later College of Liberal Arts offices (Anthropology); proposed for closure
style: Early-20th-century brick collegiate (hip roof, dormers, arched corner porch in early photos)
statusNote: Phase 1 closure list, Oct 2025; Anthropology moved to Huddleston

facts.text: Built with a 1902 state appropriation as the agricultural and horticultural building; the third floor went unfinished until 1914 for lack of funds.
Named for U.S. Senator Justin Smith Morrill of Vermont, author of the Morrill Act that created land-grant colleges.
One of six Durham buildings UNH proposed in October 2025 to close in a first phase, chosen on cost of ownership, condition and occupancy.
The Anthropology Department's contact page now gives Huddleston Hall 328 as its office.

verdict: Handsome 1903 hip-roofed brick hall named for the land-grant act's author, never majorly renovated and now emptied for closure.
notes: Old data said it housed Education and Anthropology; Anthropology has moved to Huddleston Hall 328 (search snippets still show 'B11 Morrill Hall', from an older version of the page). No major renovation documented. Whether the closure was carried out is unconfirmed (TNH, Dec 2025: Phase 1 targeted Jan/Jun 2026, not confirmed). No licensed modern photo found; only historic images. Archives ref-01 is a 1917 Clement Moran photo. Designer unknown. No reviews.
judgeNotes: Only historic images; condition and function low for the closure.
